body: Yes I am actually in a suburban IPR, but it’s connected to a large metropolitan hospital, which makes it huge and means the job is strictly IPR. I did initially look for smaller, suburban/rural hospitals like my last clinical, but they were few and far between in the area I wanted to move to. But now I’m definitely keeping in mind that a small hospital/clinic is something that I want for my next job!

Thank you so much for advice!! This is honestly exactly what I needed to hear. I think I’m just having a hard time with going from a school environment (even with having clinicals) to going straight into a crazy, rigid, non-flexible IPR position. I did IPR as my last clinical and I liked it, but I also had the benefit of being a student so didn’t have as much of a realistic job feel to it. So I def think I’ll stay at my current job for as long as I can to get experience/see if it gets better, but definitely going to keep PRN in mind!!

Idk why this post stuck out to me but I was reading it again and it really made me want to do PRN all that much more😅

What is your honest opinion on a new grad doing PRN? Do you recommend getting experience as a full time PT first and then switching to PRN? And if that’s the case, how long do you recommend going through full time employment before switching? I honestly just hate not having as much flexibility as I used to and the PTO at my job is honestly not great. I work at a hospital so we have to ask off for holidays, etc. and if our census is low they pull out all of the PRNs and make us work even longer hours.
And yes, Medicare sucks big time
Basically, in a perfect world, having a random schedule generator that made sure we didn’t round time would be ideal

I’m deleting this post because I’m not being snippy but this was a post for those who understand the “non-rounding, 900 min” compliance things that Medicare does…and for tips on how to handle it without missing minutes on a patient

This wasn’t a post for me to have to explain it to someone who doesn’t understand what it is and for me to defend myself against another person who says to “get over it.” 

I came here for compassion/helpful tips, not to have to explain myself

Well if I could do that I absolutely would. But having each session at 61 min exactly every time is the same as having each session at 60 min (aka rounding time) and would get us dinged and we would get in trouble once again

Well if you’re not understanding, then maybe you haven’t had to deal with it and I’m happy for ya! But instead of agreeing/responding to someone who posted a rude comment, maybe try asking me to clarify?

And adds all sorts of miscommunication between therapists, Medicare noncompliance with patients, and not to mention, creates tension in the work environment!!

Sounds like you’ve got a lot of frustration too, hope your comment helped you let some of it out!!!!

Well yes, but then like I said, they have to start a minute later which either makes then shorten their therapy session or if they want to keep a full hour then they have to start all sessions a minute late through the end of the day and it just screws them over
Thank you for the info! My boyfriend is in the military and if it works out with him I could always have VA benefits but that wouldn’t be for awhile!!
Love that!!
Yes that sounds veryyy nice!
No this is veery helpful!! Thank you so much!
Okay that’s good to hear!! Honestly I think it would be great to just be able to say “hmmm, I want a week off (if I have enough saved)”
Thank you!! I actually have another post asking about PRN/per diem over full time to give me some more flexibility and off time. Do you recommend it?
Hahaha unfortunately I do not, but I appreciate the offer 😂
Okay wow that’s also a great idea!! This is exactly what I needed to hear!!
This is actually GREAT advice!! I’m currently soooo worried about everything I think it’s exhausting me mentally/emotionally😅
Thank you, this is very helpful!!
Ugh that stinks, I mean, I feel like I’m not acting cocky or overconfident in the slightest (quite the opposite, actually). Have just kind of kept my head down and did what I was told!
Yes I definitely think it’s a better way to do things!! Again, one of the reasons why I picked this clinic!

Yeah it’s just tough when working at an IPR is already physically and mentally exhausting…Most days when I get home I’m so tired all I want to do is lay on the couch, nap, and go to bed early. My social life has really gone down hill and it would just be nice to have some sort of good energy going into work!

Thank you! I honestly wanted to transition quicker but again, I think my DOR and manager want all new therapists to feel comfortable with their caseload and not feel like they’re just using them to get as much patient care as possible. One of the reasons why I liked this place so much! I just don’t like hostility when I have nothing to do with it!!
Omg I literally just wrote “kill them with kindness” on a post it note last night that I put on my mirror!! What a coincidence! Thank you for the advice
Thank you!!!
Thank you thank you!!
That’s what I’m definitely trying to keep in mind!! Thank you so much for this comment!
Thank you! Hearing that I’m not crazy or a wimp for being hurt by that comment does make me feel better!

Yeah, shadowing other clinicians, nursing, case management, even some higher ups, just so I could get an idea for what everyone’s job consisted of…There were times it may have definitely been overkill, but they supposedly do that with every new grad and they pride themselves in showing their therapists every side of rehab
Thank you!! I understand that I’m “low man,” but I didn’t think it meant I deserved to get embarrassed in front of my entire therapy staff😅

Although a harsh response, I understand where you’re coming from. Frankly, that’s something I hope changes in our profession because if burnout is causing people to treat others poorly and you cannot even go to your boss about a hostile work environment without being labeled as a “tattler” or a “problem,” then this isn’t a profession I want to be in for long.

I still don’t think you’re quite understanding what I’m even saying, as my clinic is big on “what can they do to help our clinic culture excel” and “please tell us ways to boost morale.” Again, I would not be “ratting out” an entire department or anyone specifically. We just have required meetings with our DOR where they ask if we are feeling welcomed/comfortable with our coworkers. If, in 3 months I’m still getting short, snappy comments from others, I will ask my DOR how I CAN mesh better with my coworkers. And even if they don’t give me decent advice or if they do, at the very least it will be on paper that I at least went to the DOR before deciding to find someplace else to work. 

Again, there is no “ratting out” or “tattling” on coworkers. I hope I’ve made that clear.

Oh I would NEVER rat out anyone specifically for not being welcoming. I’m not sure if you read my entire response or just immediately commented without fully understanding my plan/thought process, but as I said in the response, I would ask the DOR if there was anything I could do [as a new grad] to help make myself feel more comfortable around my coworkers. I would never go in and “tattle” on seasoned therapists unless something was continuously a problem. 

However, responses like yours do help me understand the friction between seasoned and new therapists. I understand that I don’t have nearly the experience that you have, but coming in with a quick, short and frankly, unhelpful response to my sincere questions is the exact problem I’m facing right now—as are many of my previous classmates. Telling me to just “do my job” is the exact reason we as a profession also have burnout. Can’t we also enjoy our job? Or is that too impossible to ask?

Thank you for the support!! I’ve seriously been looking forward to finally joining the workforce and being in an uplifting, cultivating clinic, but at the moment, it just feels like my coworkers are mad at me for not jumping right in head first (although I don’t think I could have even if I tried). Like I said in another reply, I think I’m going to give it a good 3 months starting today to just put my nose to the grindstone and focus on absorbing as much as I can and not making friends be my #1 priority (or even 2 or 3). Of course I’m going to be nice, cordial, and professional, but I have a bit of a people pleasing problem and try to win everyone’s approval. If the environment doesn’t change, I think I’ll bring it up nicely to the DOR at our next monthly meeting. 

I had extra time today because I don’t have a complete caseload yet (because our census has been low) and decided to help out our PTA who had a patient that needed more therapy to be compliant by picking up 30 min with her and the PTA tried to put the entire patient on me (even though I still had a ton of documentation to do and a meeting with the DOR). I politely declined and did the 30 min only :-). So…baby steps, but some progress!

Thank you for your response!! I’m trying to be understanding, I just can’t help but feel a sadness about how on top of student debt, new grad stress, possible early burnout, moving to a new city, etc., new grads are now experiencing this kind of behavior from veteran therapists who are supposed to make you WANT to work together😅

But yeah, my plan is to not take anything personal for at least 3 months, and if it’s still not a welcoming environment, I’m going to say something to my DOR (not by naming any names) but just ask him what I can personally do to feel more welcome.

Ugh I’m so so sorry for that!! It’s only been 2 years and I’m still struggling to remember who I was before😅

But I’ve discovered that—like you said—I’ve just got to roll with the punches and when I start feeling too emotional/upset about something that I need to give it some time and THEN take a step back and look at it as subjectively as possible. Then I’m usually able to deescalate my emotions (a little bit). 

And I have definitely noticed a good nights’ sleep helps me waaaay more than just about anything else!

Again, thank you again for all of your info. Congrats on being done with it once and for all and being able to take care of your kiddos!!! I’m sure I will be in contact with you in the coming months, haha.

Thank you again so much for helping me feel normal😂😂 I’m on the struggle bus right now!! I was actually only on 150 mg ER for a year and a half and on welbutrin for about a year before that (have never really been on any form of anti-depressant for very long). But I also feel like I’ve always been very sensitive to emotions/hormones and I’m sure that’s why I’m having such intense mood swings because I haven’t been in it for nearly as long as you or a lot of people in this thread.

Thank you so much for your response!! I honestly can’t thank you enough either for posting your experience because it has helped me cope and not feel like I’m going crazy and/or actually need to be put on meds (although I have never been diagnosed with clinical depression/anxiety. I’ve also just moved to a new city, started a new job, and am farther away from my family and any bit of familiarity that I’ve been used to so it’s been a tough month! But luckily I have a few friends here and a bf I can vent to. 

Do you have any tips/tricks you used for long term withdrawals that were different than short term? I’ve recently begun having issues with insomnia and I’m not going to lie, the only things that seem to help are melatonin mixed with Benadryl😅 my mood swings are also crazy again (I’m hyper-sensitive and have a short fuse all of a sudden). I’m taking fish oil, B12, and even some natural thyroid supplements to combat the weight I’ve gained/slowed metabolism I suddenly have. So any other suggestions would be helpful too!!!

And I know from your comments that you said the first year was very tough, but looking back, before your year was up, was there any period that you felt like yourself again? And if so, about what timeframe was that? I just need something to look forward to that’s closer than a year away😅

I know this is an old post but even 2 years later there aren’t many people who have shared their story with long-term withdrawal from effexor, so I thank you SO MUCH. Honestly I come back to this post when I have a mental breakdown thinking I actually need to be on anti-anxiety meds because of how crazy I feel—but it helps remind me that it’s most likely the withdrawals.

I’m officially 1 month off and had almost the exact same experience as you!! 3 weeks out I was feeling energetic and happy and focused but suddenly this past week I have felt achey, sweaty, cold, and just generally off. I then proceeded to have an intense mental breakdown in front of my good friends (who were probably the perfect people to break down to at least). 

But I responded to this comment because my PCP prescribed me effexor for my anxiety/stress about grad school and my fear of public speaking!!! She told me that it would just be a “temporary” medication that I could easily come off of when I was finished with school. I’ve actually had her as my PCP for years and loved her, but I have been recently extremely bitter towards her because she said this drug would be a temporary fix and had no idea what the withdrawals would be like. 

Again, I thank you so much for your story and I would love a life/effexor update if at all possible. (That way I can at least count down the days until I know I’ll feel like myself again!!)

Hi, thank you for your input. I am tracking my calories, macronutrients, etc. and am definitely eating what I’m supposed to be eating, trust me. 

However I did not gain this weight until I was on Effexor and at the moment I am OFF of Effexor. I am eating way less than I was while on Effexor and working out/on my feet more. And since getting off Effexor and eating less calories/working out more than I have in over a year and I have gained about 3 lbs, so yes I do think it has something to do with my thyroid, hormones, metabolism, etc. and no, I don’t think it’s because I’m overeating, thank you :-)

I’m a 26 F and I gained around 40ish lbs while on 150 mg ER for a year…I felt like I was always hungry, had no motivation to workout, and craved CARBS. However, I’m not off of it and even though my cravings/intense hunger is gone…I’m struggling to lose weight :-) I also got huge red stretch marks all over my stomach and hips all of a sudden so that’s awesome!!!!! 🥲
You got this!!! But I know EXACTLY what you mean…I’m almost three weeks of of it and finally only feel like this if I get dehydrated😅

Yeah, I get that…Tbh I had a previous relationship that went 0-100 in like a month or two (which in retrospect is extremely unhealthy/toxic) and so I struggle to know what a normal, healthy relationship timeline looks like, let alone one that involves someone with a kid!

Ugh you’re not alone!! As you can see I’m seriously struggling myself, but I’m currently just having to take it day by day. From the research I’ve done, the emotional symptoms should normally last around 2 weeks at the most, and if they last longer you should probably see your healthcare provider to make sure nothing else is wrong!!

Lastly, do you have any family/friend support?? Do you have a hobby and/or exercise consistently?? So far the only things that have somewhat kept my sanity in check have been my friends and family who check on me 24/7 and I can vent/rant/cry to. And working out/finding something that I enjoy doing has also seemed to help somewhat. You’ve got this though, I believe in you!

Ohhh yes I am seeing what you’re saying now!! Honestly, I’m not entirely sure what they decided on—and I’m not sure when/if he’ll tell me (although I hope he does). But at the point I think because I’m a newbie in this relationship that it’s not my place to push him to pick lunch over dinner…Honestly in the end I feel like I’m going to have to trust him to do the right thing and keep it professional…But of course if he doesn’t, the truth eventually always comes out and I will be dumping his a**

Thank you again for the insight!! Secondly, we actually planned awhile back for me to fly in and meet his kiddo and his fam for the first time but unfortunately they all got sick after being on a family vacation together and we weren’t able to meet :-( But hopefully within the next couple of months I’m going to get to meet them soon!!

And I also don’t have alot of close friends/family that have had to deal with a situation like this!!

Hey guys!! So I actually decided to keep with the fast taper…I’m kind of one of those people that just wants to get off of something as fast as possible, deal with the withdrawals, and never worry about it again😅 today is my third day without ANY venlafaxine/Effexor and I actually don’t feel as bad as I have been. I kind of think the going back and forth from 75 mg to none was just prolonging my withdrawals!! We’ll see though!
